item: Row 383: a committing import holds the re-index drain's start until it ends, so the swap never waits 180 s for a drain and refuses
summary: A committing restore stops the re-index drain at its writer checks (R659), but a drain started after the last check (the boot's last step, the Resume button, a hand-off) took its lease batch after batch; the swap's barrier polls every 0.25 s and could miss the gap between batches, so it waited its whole 180 s and refused the import with another job is still writing ... import again. run_restore with commit=True now opens a hold before its first writer check and closes it on every way out (a decorator, beside _settle_pending_net). Inside it, start() on a stops_for_restore job starts nothing, remembers the ask and raises StartHeldForRestore (a RuntimeError, so every caller reads it as not started now; the Resume route also answers held_for_import: true). The check and the start sit under one lock with the hold's opening, so a drain that got in first is running at the check and is stopped by it. When the hold ends the held start is made, through start() again, unless an import run's window is open (the run starts the drain once, when it ends) or the app began shutting down since the ask; an earlier cancel does not drop it, since the ask came after. The hold wraps the safety net's settlement (it compares the live store, which a drain could change). A restart by another restore that ends meanwhile (_start_again) is held the same way, under the same lock order. The task manager's Resume answers its existing busy 409 for a held start, and the hand-off reports a drain the held start already made as started. A restore that does not commit holds nothing; writers that are not stops_for_restore jobs keep the stated limit. Race test: a thread starting the drain over and over while the hold opens and the check stops it never sees the drain run after the check. No schema change, no new string.
